title: Cultivation Safety, Legal Boundaries and Responsible Practice
summary: Cultivation education must distinguish plant-science knowledge from legal authorization and place worker, household and emergency safety ahead of crop-preservation goals or production convenience.

sections.title: Legal authority depends on jurisdiction
sections.body: Cannabis and hemp rules can differ by country, state, tribal jurisdiction, license type, product and growing location. Educational content should teach learners how to identify the controlling authority rather than treating one national or neighboring-state rule as permission.

sections.title: Agricultural and controlled-environment work carries hazards
sections.body: Heat, machinery, electrical equipment, chemicals, lifting and repetitive work can affect cultivation operations. Controls should follow qualified equipment instructions and applicable occupational rules rather than improvised production shortcuts.

sections.title: Product evidence and legal authorization are separate
sections.body: A pesticide or biological treatment can have scientific evidence and still be prohibited for a specific cannabis use or jurisdiction. Conversely, a legal product claim does not eliminate the need for diagnosis, label compliance and efficacy monitoring.
